郷.meaning: A clanking <part>robot</part> on a space station finds a child's <part>scribble</part> taped inside its locker: a crayon village with a <part>pennant</part> flapping on the school roof. Its eyes flicker. It was built in that very village. It books the next rocket down to its <kanji>home town</kanji>.
郷.on: At the rocket desk it tells the clerk where it was built: '<sound>Kyo</sound>to,' stretching the start like a long, happy beep.
郷.kun: Back home, the school cook hands it a <sound>sa</sound>rdine on a stick, and the children dance round the old <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

匂.meaning: A chef enters a cooking contest blindfolded. He can't see the dishes, so he lifts the cloth <part>wrap</part> off each pot and holds a <part>spoon</part> under his nose. One whiff of the soup and he sighs and faints into the judge's lap. It's that <kanji>fragrant</kanji>.
匂.kun: The judge drops her <sound>nee</sound>dle and thread and cries, '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

摘.meaning: A lighthouse keeper can't reach the cherries on the tree below her cliff. Each night, by the glow of a <part>hanging lantern</part>, she lowers a tiny <part>anchor</part> on a fishing line, snags one stalk and reels it up. One cherry at a time is how she likes to <kanji>pluck</kanji>.
摘.on: She sends her sister a <sound>tex</sound>t message with a photo of every cherry.
摘.kun: When a cherry falls on her nose she sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a <sound>moo</sound>se below catches it.

鑑.meaning: A museum guard has one job: to <part>oversee</part> a single glass case. Inside, pinned on velvet, is a beetle of solid <part>gold</part>, the only one ever found. He hasn't blinked in years, and some nights it winks back. Scientists fly in just to peer at the <kanji>specimen</kanji>.
鑑.on: Each visitor leaves a pink <sound>car</sound>nation by the case.
鑑.kun: Its label is written in <sound>car</sound>nation-pink ink, beside a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic to keep the moths away.

疾.meaning: Rain drips through a <part>leaky shed</part> where an old man plays darts alone. A drip falls, he throws a <part>dart</part> and pins it to the wall before it hits the floor. Then the next, and the next. His arm is a blur. Nothing moves so <kanji>rapidly</kanji>.
疾.on: He hangs a bed <sound>shee</sound>t on the wall to catch the darts.
疾.kun: His cat watches from a little <sound>hu</sound>t of boxes, batting a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn just as fast.

禅.meaning: A street <part>lamppost</part> grows tired of the city's noise. It stops flickering, stops buzzing, and makes its whole life <part>simple</part>: one steady light, no thoughts. Moths land on it and fall asleep, and even the pigeons whisper. The lamppost has found <kanji>Zen</kanji>.
禅.on: Each night it lights a tiny <sound>zen</sound> garden at its foot, the sand raked into circles.
禅.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p dozes under it, a yu<sound>zu</sound> rolls by without a bump, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the gutter doesn't splash: all quiet.

鼓.meaning: A beaver finds an old <part>drum</part> washed down the river. Having no sticks, she snaps a <part>branch</part> off an alder and starts thumping. Every animal in the valley comes to dance on the dam. She gives up building for good and spends her days on the <kanji>drum</kanji>.
鼓.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala keeps time by thumping its tail on a log.
鼓.kun: The dust makes her sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a yu<sound>zu</sound> bounces off the drum onto a <sound>mee</sound>rkat's head.

妃.meaning: A <part>woman</part> who charms snakes at the fair plays her flute, and a <part>cobra</part> rises from the basket, coils round her head and spreads its hood like a jewelled crown. The crowd bows without knowing why. For that one tune, she's a <kanji>queen</kanji>.
妃.on: She bows back and wobbles on one tall <sound>hee</sound>l.
妃.kun: Her purse holds a gold <sound>key</sound>, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine for the snake and a second <sound>key</sound> for the basket.

戯.meaning: A bored knight stands guard over a <part>void</part>, a great empty hole where the castle used to be. Nobody's coming, so he plants his <part>spear</part>, swings round it like a dancer and turns cartwheels by the edge. The crows join in. On duty, he can't help but <kanji>frolic</kanji>.
戯.on: The rusty <sound>gear</sound> in his visor whirs as he spins.
戯.kun: He lands in a <sound>tu</sound>b of rainwater, yells '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and a <sound>moo</sound>se laughs at him.

悟.meaning: A quiz champion stares at the last riddle for six hours while her <part>heartbeat</part> races. Suddenly the answer pops into her head like toast. She leaps up and smacks a <part>high five</part> on the startled host's hand. At last she can <kanji>perceive</kanji> what it meant.
悟.on: She pulls off the swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles she wore all night to stay focused.
悟.kun: Her prize: a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines, a little <sound>to</sound>tem pole and a tame <sound>roo</sound>k.

努.meaning: A <part>guy</part> at the fair bets he can tow a bus with a rope in his teeth. His face goes red, every <part>muscle</part> shakes, and the bus creeps forward an inch an hour. By sunset it has crossed the car park. He's never worked so hard: a whole day of <kanji>toil</kanji>.
努.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin in the harbour claps its flippers for him.
努.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and leans on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to rest.

騎.meaning: At the riding show, a <part>horse</part> trots into the ring with something <part>strange</part> on its back: a goldfish in a bowl, wearing a tiny hat. It clears every fence without spilling a drop. The judges give the fish first prize for <kanji>equestrian</kanji> skill.
騎.on: Afterwards the fish reaches into the saddlebag for a tiny <sound>key</sound> and winds up the horse: it was clockwork all along.

凹.meaning: A plump hen likes to nap on top of an upside-down <part>bucket</part>. Every day she's a little heavier, and the metal sags, until there's a cosy dip shaped exactly like her. Now she lays her eggs in it. The bucket's top is <kanji>concave</kanji>.
凹.on: She drags it into the shade of a huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and acorns roll into the dip.
凹.kun: The <sound>he</sound>n shares her dip with a lost <sound>ko</sound>ala.

僚.meaning: At the office trip in the woods, everyone hangs their jackets on one <part>coat hook</part> nailed to a pine and sits round a <part>bonfire</part>. The grumpy man from accounts shares his marshmallows and tells jokes. Out here he isn't the boss's spy; he's your <kanji>colleague</kanji>.
僚.on: Afterwards the whole team sleeps on mats at a quiet <sound>ryo</sound>kan.

裕.meaning: A farmer's <part>weathervane</part> spins to point at the <part>valley</part> whenever good weather is coming. One spring it never stops pointing. Rain at night, sun by day, pumpkins the size of cars. He gives fruit away to every stranger. The harvest is <kanji>abundant</kanji>.
裕.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots down from the hills to help carry the pumpkins.

拓.meaning: A sailor wants a garden on a rocky island. He ties his <part>anchor</part> to a rope and swings it like a hammer, smashing each <part>stone</part> to gravel and dragging the bits into the sea. By autumn there's bare earth for carrots. It took a year to <kanji>clear</kanji> the land.
拓.on: He celebrates with a crunchy <sound>taco</sound> on the first flat patch.
拓.kun: His wife cheers from the boat, kicking up one high <sound>hee</sound>l: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

凶.meaning: In a quiet barbershop, a <part>bucket</part> of fresh flowers stands by the door. Every night someone sneaks in with a pair of <part>scissors</part> and snips the heads off. The barber sets a trap and catches him: the mayor, in a mask. A small but real <kanji>villain</kanji>.
凶.on: He tries to slip away on the train, shouting '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!' and stretching the start, but trips over the bucket.

抽.meaning: A dentist has lost her pliers, so she ties a tiny <part>anchor</part> to a string, hooks it round a crocodile's wobbly tooth and pulls. Out it pops, with a note stuck to it giving the <part>reason</part> for the ache: 'Too many sweets.' The oddest tooth she's had to <kanji>pluck</kanji>.
抽.on: The crocodile had been <sound>chew</sound>ing gum for a week, and it's still stuck to the tooth.
抽.kun: To say thanks, the crocodile hands her one high <sound>hee</sound>l and a <sound>key</sound> to the swamp.

抹.meaning: A ship's painter writes THE <part>end</part> in huge letters on the hull, then the captain says the voyage will go on. So the painter hangs off the <part>anchor</part> chain with a sponge and scrubs the letters away one by one. It takes him all night to <kanji>rub</kanji> them out.
抹.on: Two scruffy <sound>mutts</sound> on deck chase the soap bubbles he makes.

謡.meaning: A shy monk is asked to give a <part>speech</part> at a picnic, so he sings it instead, slow and low, tapping time with a <part>can opener</part> on the bean tins. The ants stop to listen and the ducks hum along. The whole picnic turns into a <kanji>chant</kanji>.
謡.on: A boy at the back keeps the beat with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, up and down, slowly.
謡.kun: Afterwards everyone slurps <sound>u</sound>don from one big <sound>tu</sound>b.

腸.meaning: An astronaut on the <part>moon</part> eats a whole crate of space noodles under the <part>sunbeams</part>. Soon a long, twisty rumble travels round and round inside her belly, like a train in a tunnel. Mission control hears it on the radio and worries about her <kanji>intestines</kanji>.
腸.on: The doctor on the radio tells her to loosen her tight <sound>cho</sound>ker.
腸.kun: Back home she rests in a <sound>hu</sound>t, the crew cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!', a baby cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and she soaks in a warm <sound>tu</sound>b.

魅.meaning: A <part>ghost</part> haunts a young apple tree that has <part>not yet</part> grown its first fruit. Every night it sits in the branches, staring and waiting. Weeks pass. It forgets to rattle chains or scare anyone. A ghost that can't stop watching a tree: that's <kanji>fascination</kanji>.
魅.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands beside it, staring at the tree just as hard.

唐.meaning: Under an old <part>shed</part>, a gardener leans his <part>rake</part> on a <part>pole</part> and digs up <part>one</part> painted vase with a dragon's open <part>mouth</part> on its side. A museum man runs in, shaking: it's a thousand years old, from the great dynasty of the <kanji>T'ang</kanji>.
唐.on: The gardener drops it on his <sound>toe</sound>, but the vase doesn't even crack.
唐.kun: A painted <sound>ca</sound>rp swims round its neck, and the museum man cheers, '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

逐.meaning: A <part>pig</part> escapes the farm and races up a wooden <part>ramp</part> onto the ferry. The farmer chases it, then the dog, then grandma on her scooter. The ferry sails off with all of them aboard, still running laps round the deck. That pig is hard to <kanji>pursue</kanji>.
逐.on: It runs on a bag of <sound>chick</sound>pea crisps it stole from the galley.

恨.meaning: A <part>robot</part> butler dropped the birthday cake thirty years ago, and the whole family laughed. Every time it hears that laugh, its <part>heartbeat</part> monitor spikes. It still polishes the forks, but slowly, wishing it could take that day back. Even metal can carry <kanji>regret</kanji>.
恨.on: It tells its troubles only to a giant <sound>con</sound>dor that perches on the chimney.
恨.kun: It serves the family cold <sound>u</sound>don, and won't join in when they cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

覆.meaning: A racing yacht heading <part>west</part> hits a wave and flips upside down. The crew can't <part>restore</part> it, so they stand on the hull and keep going, steering with an umbrella while fish wave up at them. It's the first race ever won after a <kanji>capsize</kanji>.
覆.on: A crane on the dock lowers a big <sound>hook</sound> and turns the boat right way up.
覆.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>,' groan the fish as the sail flops over them like a blanket: to cover.

惜.meaning: A museum cleaner dusts a jar from <part>antiquity</part> that has survived floods, fires and wars. She sneezes. Her <part>heartbeat</part> skips as the jar wobbles, tips and breaks in two. Three thousand years, undone by one sneeze. What a <kanji>pity</kanji>.
惜.on: The guide's pie chart of museum accidents gets a new <sound>sec</sound>tor: sneezes.
惜.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' she whispers, and starts gluing the halves.

陳.meaning: A junk shop faces the <part>east</part>, so at dawn the rising sun lights its window like a stage. Under a faded <part>pennant</part>, the owner sets out his oddest stock: a stuffed walrus in a tutu, a glass eye, a sofa shaped like a shoe. Crowds press their noses to the town's best <kanji>exhibit</kanji>.
陳.on: The walrus has a painted moustache and a very big <sound>chin</sound>.
陳.kun: The owner turns the shoe sofa by its <sound>hee</sound>l, hangs a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t on it and perches a stuffed <sound>roo</sound>k on top: a twist.

兼.meaning: A juggler balances on <part>one</part> leg on top of a <part>pole</part>. On his head sits a helmet with two <part>horns</part>, each spinning a plate; he waves a <part>rake</part> in one hand and kicks <part>eight</part> balls into the air with his free foot, all at once. Every trick happens <kanji>concurrently</kanji>.
兼.on: His dog barks along from its <sound>ken</sound>nel at the foot of the pole.
兼.kun: On the tip of the rake he balances a bowl with a <sound>ca</sound>rp in it.

妨.meaning: A <part>woman</part> paints the sunset from her little boat. Every time she lifts her brush, the <part>sail</part> swings round and blocks the view. She ties it, it flaps loose; she lowers it, the wind lifts it. Not one stroke all evening. Nothing could <kanji>disturb</kanji> her more.
妨.on: Then a <sound>bou</sound>lder rolls off the cliff and splashes her canvas.
妨.kun: A gull drops a <sound>sa</sound>rdine in her <sound>mu</sound>g, then sits in her paint <sound>tu</sound>b.
